questions.prompt: What does the OpenAI Agents SDK's default trace record for a run?

options.text: Only the final text returned to the user at the end.
options.explanation: A trace is a record of the whole run, not only the last message.

options.text: Model calls, tool calls, handoffs and guardrails.
options.explanation: Right. The docs list these, plus any custom spans you add, shown in the Traces dashboard.

options.text: Only the daily token total for your whole organization.
options.explanation: That is a usage report. A trace shows the steps of one run.

questions.prompt: A dashboard reads the Claude Usage and Cost API. What fits the docs?

options.text: Poll every second, since the API is built for live counters.
options.explanation: The docs support polling once per minute for sustained use. Faster polling is fine only for short bursts.

options.text: Poll about once a minute, cache results, and expect a short delay.
options.explanation: Right. Data typically appears within 5 minutes, and the docs suggest caching results for dashboards.

options.text: Call it once a month, because data appears after the billing cycle ends.
options.explanation: Usage data typically appears within 5 minutes of a request, not after the cycle.

questions.prompt: Where should a per-prompt id such as prompt.id go in your telemetry?

options.text: On every metric as a label, so each prompt has its own line.
options.explanation: Claude Code keeps such ids off metrics because they would cause unbounded cardinality and raise storage cost.

options.text: On events and log lines, where one prompt's records join.
options.explanation: Right. Claude Code puts prompt.id on events, so you can filter one prompt's records. Metrics stay low-cardinality.

options.text: In the metric name, so dashboards sort by prompt in a list.
options.explanation: A new name per prompt is the same cardinality problem in a different place.
